title: C compress emits non-IPv6/short input as Rule255 while Python/Rust reject - mixed-fleet blackhole
description: P2, found independently by all three codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk (kimi correctness, kimi edge-cases, worker5 subagent security). lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c:542-555: any pkt_len < 40 or version != 6 input is emitted verbatim as 0xFF + raw bytes (raw uncompressed fallback branch, predates the fix). Python compress_packet (headers.py:860) and Rust compress (codec.rs:2160 -> validate_full_ipv6_structure codec.rs:272-277) both reject non-IPv6 input instead. Probe: 3-byte garbage -> C rc=4 rule=0xff; 45-byte IPv4-shaped buffer -> C ACCEPT ret=46 rule=255 while Python raises (version must be 6). Same blackhole shape bead hahk closed for malformed IPv6: C emits Rule255 datagrams every Rust/Python peer fatals on at ingress decode_rule255. Pure-C fleets round-trip it (C RX rule255 branch lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c:152-165 does no payload validation), masking the divergence. No vector in test/vectors/schc_compression.json covers non-IPv6 input (all malformed_input packets start 0x60). Fix: reject non-IPv6 like the references, or deliberately re-contract the C-only passthrough and pin it; either way add malformed_input vectors (short garbage, version-4) and rerun scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py. Reachability low (in-tree callers feed IPv6) hence P2 not P1.
close_reason: Fixed and pinned. lichen_schc_compress (lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c) now rejects non-IPv6 input - pkt_len < IPV6_HDR_LEN or version nibble != 6 returns SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT (-6) instead of emitting 0xFF+raw bytes as Rule255, closing the mixed-fleet blackhole where a C node emitted datagrams every Rust/Python peer fatals on at decode_rule255. Error-code choice: -6 is the existing shared-enum value already used for contract violations (NULL packet) and is distinct from BUFFER_TOO_SMALL; all callers (lichen_link_tx.c:136-138, lichen_l2_tx.c:149-157, bridge lichen_l2.c:988-996) handle <0 generically, so no caller churn. The rule255 raw-emit branch previously guarded an overflow check that became dead with the emit removed. References aligned: python compress_packet raises SchcError for len<40 (headers.py:142-145) and version!=6 (packet.py:116-117); rust compress -> validate_full_ipv6_structure raises InvalidPacket (codec.rs:272-277). Pinned by two new shared malformed_input vectors in test/vectors/schc_compression.json: non_ipv6_short_input_malformed (deadbeef) and non_ipv6_version4_input_malformed (45-byte version-4 datagram whose internal length fields are self-consistent) - consumed by python test_schc_vector (pytest.raises SchcError), rust shared_vectors (compress is_err), C parity check_malformed_input (negative return + untouched output sentinel). C host test test_uncompressed_fallback (which pinned the abolished raw-emit behavior by round-tripping deadbeef as Rule255 - that was the bug) replaced by test_reject_non_ipv6_input asserting SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT for both classes. Gates on heft: C host schc suite 15/15 (clang, ASan/UBSan); C schc_parity 51 vectors PASS; python test_vectors.py 772/772; rust shared_vectors 3/3 (scratch worktree, oscore path redirected, not committed); cppcheck clean on schc.c. Codereview 3x per step 4 (reviewer model): correctness kimi-k3 PASS (no remaining Rule255-for-non-IPv6 path - the profile-agnostic engine fallback's sole production caller is the gated lichen_schc_compress; short-circuit ordering prevents OOB; vector hex verified programmatically; consumers verified, python executed); edge-cases kimi-k3 PASS (pkt_len 0/39/40 boundaries, version-6-garbage still validator-rejected, reject path never consults out_len nor writes out, decompress TX/RX split untouched, valid-IPv6 fallback vectors unaffected); security: claude-opus-4-5 down (err_25030582) so kimi-k3 fallback ran per protocol - PASS (engine fallback has exactly one gated production caller, other fallback profiles are test/fuzz-only, relay re-emission has no production callers and matches rust semantics, -6 handled by all callers, vector shape unambiguous). Adjacent pre-existing gaps confirmed already tracked, not re-filed: C RX rule255 laxness (lqgt/5rvk), ceiling off-by-one (1npp), endpoint policy (wrxl), corpus schema validation (ojzg), crash_info mislabel (yvu8).
